The launch extends a run of JPYC integrations on Polygon, which now processes more JPYC volume than all other chains combined.

title: US Sanctions Iranian Marine Insurers Taking Bitcoin for Strait of Hormuz Passage
blurb: The US Treasury's OFAC sanctioned two Iranian firms, HormuzSafe Marine Services and the Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company, for running an IRGC-backed scheme that forces commercial vessels to buy transit "insurance" for the Strait of Hormuz, with HormuzSafe accepting Bitcoin and other digital assets to evade sanctions. The designations block all US-based assets and expose non-US counterparties to secondary sanctions, extending a pattern of Iranian state entities routing to crypto rails as banking channels close.

title: Strategy books $8.2 billion Q2 loss on bitcoin price decline
blurb: Strategy (MSTR) reported an $8.2 billion Q2 net loss, driven almost entirely by an $8.32 billion unrealized markdown on its 843,775 bitcoin under fair-value accounting, now worth about $54.8 billion against a $63.7 billion cost basis. The firm has built a $3.75 billion cash reserve covering 2.1 years of preferred dividends and started selling bitcoin under a new monetization program.

title: South Korea plans to tax crypto gains over $1,740 as political battle moves to parliament
blurb: South Korea will begin taxing crypto gains above 2.5 million won ($1,740) at a combined 22% rate starting January 1, 2027, after officials signaled they will not delay the measure a fourth time. The rules bar loss carry-forwards, which critics warn could push domestic investors toward offshore exchanges and P2P markets, though a March bill to abolish the tax remains in subcommittee.

title: Demystifying Solana Bots: From GitHub Blueprints to On-Chain Fingerprints
blurb: A new empirical study maps Solana's bot ecosystem across 586 GitHub repositories and 200 on-chain addresses spanning over 44 million transactions, deriving a taxonomy of 15 bot categories across five domains including trading, MEV, and on-chain analytics. The authors identify a shared five-stage operational pipeline behind most implementations and document how bots leave distinct on-chain execution fingerprints across trading platforms and assets. Bot-driven DEX activity topped $250M in daily volume in January 2026.

title: Bipartisan Sens. Tillis and Gallego send new ethics compromise to White House in Clarity Act push
blurb: Sens. Thom Tillis and Ruben Gallego sent a revised ethics compromise to the White House on Thursday, aiming to unblock the Clarity Act crypto market-structure bill before the Senate's Aug. 7 recess. The bill still lacks the 60 votes needed, with a contested sunset clause that would expire the ethics restrictions in January 2029 and hand enforcement to Trump's acting attorney general.

title: The economics behind Aave proposal to ditch 6 chains that earn loose change in revenue
blurb: Aave governance is weighing a proposal to fully exit six low-usage chains — Sonic, Scroll, zkSync, Metis, Soneium, and Aptos — while retiring 50 asset markets and 21 expired Pendle tokens across its deployments. The six chains hold about $98M in deposits but under 1% of Aave's $14B in assets and generate less than $5,000 each per quarter, below the cost of running price feeds and liquidation systems.

title: Judge blocks Minnesota ban on prediction markets
blurb: A federal judge granted a preliminary injunction blocking Minnesota's first-of-its-kind prediction markets ban, letting Kalshi and Polymarket keep operating in the state while the case proceeds. Judge Katherine Menendez found the platforms likely to win on their claim that the federal Commodity Exchange Act preempts the state statute, a ruling that strengthens the industry's argument for exclusive CFTC jurisdiction over event contracts.

title: Senate Democrats propose anti-corruption bureau as Trump’s crypto portfolio draws more scrutiny
blurb: Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer introduced the Anti-Corruption Bureau Creation Act, a bill establishing an independent seven-member agency with subpoena and enforcement powers to investigate and claw back profits from executive branch corruption. The proposal targets President Trump's alleged conflicts of interest, including crypto ventures like World Liberty Financial that Bloomberg estimates have generated roughly $620 million for his family.

title: SIP-5: Opt-In Quantum Resistance for All Accounts
blurb: SIP-5 proposes opt-in quantum resistance for all Sei accounts, letting users migrate to post-quantum signature schemes without a forced network-wide upgrade. The additive design keeps existing ECDSA-signed accounts working while giving holders who want protection against future quantum attacks a path to harden their keys.

title: JPMorgan says crypto bill’s fading odds hurt outlook, warns parts could discourage institutional adoption
blurb: JPMorgan analysts said the Clarity Act's fading odds of passing the Senate before year-end are a setback for crypto markets, removing a near-term catalyst for regulatory clarity on token classification. The bank also warned that specific provisions in the bill could discourage institutional adoption rather than encourage it, complicating the case for large allocators waiting on federal rules before entering.

title: Quantum Solutions loses top Japan ETH treasury spot after another $1.9 million sale
blurb: Quantum Solutions sold another 1,000 ETH for roughly $1.9 million to fund its AI data center expansion, cutting its ether treasury nearly 30% since mid-June and ceding Japan's largest corporate ETH holding to Def consulting, which now holds 4,976 ETH versus Quantum's 4,765. The firm raised its sale authorization to 4,375 ETH, but 3,050 ETH is pledged as collateral to a Singapore lender, capping how much it can actually offload.

title: Stablecoin Reserve Requirements Explained
blurb: Stablecoins hold reserves to back every token in circulation, and reserve requirements set the rules for what those assets can be and how they must be managed. This guide walks through the four things every framework covers (composition, segregation, custody, and disclosure) and compares how the US GENIUS Act and the EU's MiCA implement them. Both mandate 1:1 backing in low-risk liquid assets, held separately from corporate funds and reported publicly on a regular basis.

title: IREN, Core Scientific and more surge as Aschenbrenner fund reportedly liquidates $1 billion AI infrastructure portfolio
blurb: Bitcoin miners IREN and Core Scientific surged after reports that Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness fund liquidated a roughly $1 billion portfolio built around AI infrastructure and data-center capacity. The positions reflected Aschenbrenner's thesis that power and compute buildout will gate AI scaling, and the exit sent traders scrambling to read whether the AI-datacenter bid under mining stocks is cooling.

title: ENS Scales Back Plan to Move DAO Treasury Control to New Foundation
blurb: ENS Labs revised its ENS Foundation proposal to keep the DAO's operational wallet, 54.6M ENS tokens, and the appointment of Foundation directors under tokenholder control, transferring only administration of the roughly $65M Endowment Safe after weeks of delegate opposition. Endowment transactions now pass through a timelock by default, with the Security Council holding a cancellation right, while ENS traded at $4.34, up 4.2% over 24 hours.

title: Ready Shuts Card Program After Issuer Kulipa's Sudden Wind-Down
blurb: Ready, the self-custodial wallet formerly known as Argent, shut down its card program on Wednesday after issuer Kulipa wound down without notice due to solvency issues. Kulipa, a Paris startup that ran card programs for roughly 20 wallets and fintechs, also took down Solflare's card, exposing how many crypto card products rent the same handful of issuer processors as a shared point of failure.

title: Lightning Labs Launches Site for L402 Bitcoin Agent Payments
blurb: Lightning Labs launched a dedicated website for L402, its Lightning HTTP 402 protocol, positioning the existing standard as a payment rail for AI agents to pay in bitcoin and authenticate over the Lightning Network without accounts or intermediaries. The launch pits Bitcoin-based agent payments against Coinbase's Ethereum-based x402, which recently moved to the Linux Foundation with backing from Google, Stripe, and Visa.

title: Crypto Hacks Hit Record 212 Incidents in H1 2026: Blockaid
blurb: Blockaid's H1 2026 Onchain Security Report counted a record 212 verified exploits that drained more than $1.1 billion, the highest incident count for any half-year despite dollar losses falling below H1 2025. Operational security failures like compromised keys and signing infrastructure accounted for 74% of stolen funds, while a North Korea-linked cluster led by Lazarus subgroup TraderTraitor drove 55% of all losses.

title: Range-Optimized LP Skill for Bankr Agent
blurb:
Heads up: the source is a ThreadReaderApp shell with no actual thread content — only boilerplate. Blurb below is built from the title alone; no numbers or specifics could be verified.

Bankr added a range-optimized LP skill that lets its trading agent open and rebalance concentrated liquidity positions automatically, keeping capital inside the active price band. The skill targets the manual overhead of managing Uniswap-style v3 ranges, where positions drift out of range and stop earning fees without ongoing adjustment.

title: Coinbase shares slide as revenue and earnings miss despite record market share
blurb: Coinbase reported a Q2 adjusted loss of $0.40 per share on revenue of $1.22B, down 19% year-over-year and short of analyst estimates, sending shares down more than 5% after hours as a 25% drop in spot trading volume gutted transaction revenue. Coinbase's share of global crypto trading volume still hit a record 10.3%, and average USDC held on-platform reached $20B, more than 30% of all USDC in circulation.

title: Major bitcoin wallet flaw drains 594 BTC in 25-minute sweep
blurb: An attacker drained roughly 594 BTC, worth about $38 million, from around 500 single-signature Coldcard wallets in a 25-minute sweep, exploiting a firmware flaw that skipped the device's hardware randomness generator and seeded keys from nonsecret chip data. The bug shipped in Coldcard firmware 4.0.0 in March 2021 and affects Mk3 devices on 4.0.1 or later, while Mk4, Q and Mk5 appear unaffected and bitcoin's price was little moved.

title: Quantum Solutions, Hyperscale Data tap crypto treasuries to fund AI data centers
blurb: Tokyo-listed Quantum Solutions sold 1,000 ETH for $1.9M on July 30 and raised its cumulative disposal cap to 4,375 ETH through October, funding an AI data center buildout that has cut its holdings 29% and cost it the title of Japan's largest listed ETH holder. Separately, Hyperscale Data monetized about 100 BTC and opened a bitcoin-backed credit line at 4.5%-5% to fund a Michigan AI campus.

title: Coinbase sinks 5% after missing second-quarter revenue estimates
blurb: Coinbase reported $1.22B in second-quarter revenue, missing the $1.29B consensus and down 14% quarter-over-quarter, as a crypto selloff cut spot trading volumes more than 20% and pushed shares down about 5% after hours. Transaction revenue fell to $599M and subscription and services revenue reached $555M, both short of estimates, keeping investor focus on diversification into stablecoins, Base, and prediction markets.

title: A Hardware Wallet Can Stay Offline and Still Create a Weak Seed
blurb: Coinkite warned Coldcard users on July 30 to move funds from wallets whose seed phrases were generated on a Mk3 running firmware 4.0.1 or later, after finding the seed-generation path silently fell back to a software RNG instead of the device's hardware true RNG. Coinkite estimates affected Mk3 seeds had roughly 40 bits of effective entropy rather than 128, with the Mk4, Mk5, and Q around 72 bits. Staying offline offers no protection, since the weakness lives in the seed itself and an attacker can brute-force candidate seeds on separate hardware.

title: Ondo Finance weighs acquisition worth up to $500 million
blurb: Ondo Finance is weighing an acquisition worth $250M to $500M, targeting wealthtech and other subsectors to expand its tokenized real-world assets platform, according to a person familiar with the matter. The move fits a wave of 2026 crypto consolidation, which logged $12.9B in disclosed Q2 deal value as firms buy licenses, technology, and distribution to add scale.

title: CME's Duffy warns an overlooked tax risk looms over U.S. perpetual futures
blurb: CME Group CEO Terry Duffy warned that US-approved perpetual futures could face tax ambiguity if courts or regulators classify them as swaps rather than futures, since their recurring funding payments between longs and shorts fit the statutory definition of a swap. The distinction determines whether institutional traders get Section 1256's blended 60/40 capital gains treatment or heavier ordinary-income taxation, with no IRS guidance issued and a federal court ruling on CME's challenge to the CFTC still pending.

title: JPMorgan says fading Clarity Act odds weigh on crypto outlook
blurb: JPMorgan said fading odds of the Clarity Act passing the US Senate this year remove a key regulatory catalyst for crypto, with prediction markets now implying just a 37% chance of passage before year-end. The bank warned that continued delay risks pushing tokenization onto incumbent financial infrastructure rather than public blockchains, even as institutional adoption advances via deals like Citadel Securities' $400M investment in Crypto.com.

title: Institutional crypto trading hits a record 72% as Wall Street calms crypto's wild swings
blurb: Institutions accounted for a record 72% of spot trading volume on Wintermute's OTC desk in the first half of 2026, up from about 61% in the second half of 2025. The shift has pushed realized volatility down from roughly 70% in prior cycles to around 45% and concentrated liquidity in a narrow set of tokens, making broad altcoin rallies less likely.

title: Bitcoin ETFs on track for the smallest monthly inflows ever
blurb: Bitcoin spot ETFs have drawn just $205M in net July inflows, the lowest monthly total on record, though a recovery from the $2.43B and $4.52B that exited in May and June. Ether ETFs outperformed with $342.85M for the month, tracking ETH's 11% gain against bitcoin, while XRP and Solana funds each pulled in under $14M.

title: BitRiver founder charged in Russia with $12.5 million fraud
blurb: A Russian court moved BitRiver founder Igor Runets from house arrest to a pretrial detention facility to face large-scale fraud charges tied to an unfulfilled $8M crypto mining equipment contract, with investigators alleging $12.5M in damages. The case adds to Runets' earlier tax-evasion charges as BitRiver's Siberian data center operations reel from insolvency proceedings and a six-year regional mining ban.

title: Crypto exchange Luno cuts 20% of staff amid automation push and retail trading slumps
blurb: Luno is cutting about 20% of its global workforce as weaker retail trading and increased automation reshape the DCG-owned exchange toward a leaner, more institutional model. It is the exchange's second major round of layoffs in three and a half years, following a 35% reduction in January 2023, and comes as Luno pivots toward white-label crypto infrastructure for banks and fintechs.

title: From corporation to crowd: How organizations evolved through time and technology
blurb: The a16z essay traces how organizational forms evolved to solve coordination problems, from pre-corporate merchant ventures relying on Pax Mongolica and the Lex Mercatoria to the modern corporation built for the industrial age. It argues the DUNA, a legal entity recognized in the market-structure legislation moving through Congress, is the first structure purpose-built for internet-native, protocol-governed organizations that software can now coordinate without traditional management overhead.

title: U.S. Senate puts off crypto Clarity Act for now as it focuses limited bandwidth elsewhere
blurb: The U.S. Senate shelved the crypto Clarity Act, prioritizing a Russia sanctions bill and federal nominations before its August 8 summer recess. The market structure bill remains stalled on a contentious provision barring senior officials, including President Trump, from backing crypto projects, pushing its next likely voting window to September.

title: Perceptron raises $6.5M to build decentralised AI data network
blurb: Perceptron raised $6.5M in a strategic round led by Web3 investors including Sigma Capital, Selini Capital, and QCP Capital to build a decentralized network for sourcing and verifying AI training data. The network runs over 807,000 nodes and 300,000 daily active users who contribute datasets and idle bandwidth in exchange for ownership of their data and earnings.

title: SEC and CFTC advance Project Crypto as fallback to the Clarity Act
blurb: The SEC and CFTC are advancing Project Crypto, a joint effort to define crypto assets and set rules for staking, stablecoins, custody, fundraising, and onchain trading, as the CLARITY Act stalls in Congress. The agencies have already issued a joint interpretation, with additional rules on the SEC's 2026 agenda, positioning the initiative as a regulatory workaround that cannot fully replace the stalled legislation.

title: Etherfi Cash paid out $20M in cashback on $676M of card spend
blurb: Etherfi Cash has paid out $20M in cashback across $676.3M of card spend, an effective 2.95% return distributed in USDC rather than points or a claimable token. The program has processed 8.5M transactions on 93,758 cards at a $79 average purchase, runs non-custodially, and charges 0% FX on EUR and USD spend.

title: Strategy posts $8.2 billion loss as bitcoin holdings increase 11% during Q2
blurb: Strategy reported an $8.2B net loss for Q2, driven by a mark-to-market writedown on its bitcoin holdings after the price closed the quarter more than 40% below Q2 2025 levels. The company still grew its bitcoin position 11% during the period, extending its treasury accumulation despite the paper loss weighing on reported earnings.

title: MoonPay opens PayBox for AI agent transactions
blurb: MoonPay launched PayBox, a payments layer that lets autonomous AI agents fund and settle transactions directly through the company's fiat and crypto rails. The product gives agents programmatic access to on- and off-ramps, positioning MoonPay to route machine-initiated payments as agentic commerce moves from demos toward handling real purchases and stablecoin settlement on behalf of users.

title: Stablecoins and Cross-Border Payments: How Digital Dollars Move Across Borders
blurb: Stablecoins settle cross-border payments in three legs: an on-ramp that converts local currency to a dollar-pegged token, an onchain transfer that clears in seconds to minutes, and an off-ramp back to local currency at the destination. This guide walks through the mechanics and trade-offs versus bank remittances, which stall behind compliance checks, multi-party fees, and banking hours. USDT and USDC anchor the market, together holding over 85% of stablecoin supply.

title: Fortitude targets 145% Zcash mining capacity increase with $31.5 million Bitmain order
blurb: Fortitude Mining placed a $31.5M order with Bitmain to expand its Zcash mining capacity by 145%, with the new rigs set to ship in Q4. The hardware will be deployed across the company's more than 60 MW of power capacity, concentrating its buildout on Zcash rather than Bitcoin.

title: Banco Santander Discloses Spot Bitcoin ETF Stake in 13F Filing
blurb: Banco Santander disclosed its first spot Bitcoin and Ether ETF positions in a 13F filing, reporting $4.31M in BlackRock's IBIT and $3.54M in the iShares Ethereum Trust as of June 30. The crypto holdings sit with Santander Asset Management and make up roughly 0.05% of the bank's $16.08B in reported US equity positions, adding one of Europe's largest banks to the list of TradFi institutions holding spot crypto ETFs.

title: Fake staking site drains $8.5 million in XRP from dozens of investors promising easy yield
blurb: Seoul police say a fake Flare Network staking site stole 3.4 million XRP worth about $8.5 million from 71 investors, luring them with promised monthly returns of 1.5% to 1.8%. Two suspects were detained on aggravated fraud charges and an Interpol Red Notice was requested for a third, with police estimating total losses could reach $19 million.

title: Why liquidity isn't the same as being able to settle
blurb: This thread argues that having ample liquidity is not the same as being able to settle the next obligation, because payments clear against eligible cash sitting in a specific account, not aggregate balances. A bank can hold reserves trapped in the wrong RTGS or FMI structure, own collateral stuck at a custodian, or hold dollars at the wrong correspondent after cut-off. Netting, intraday credit, repo, and FX swaps shrink the operational buffer but never eliminate it, since each still depends on haircuts, credit limits, and operating hours.

title: UK says the cloud is financial infrastructure
blurb: The UK formally designated Microsoft, Google, AWS, and Oracle as "critical third parties" to the financial sector on July 13, subjecting them to direct oversight by the Bank of England, PRA, and FCA rather than treating them as ordinary IT vendors. The framework brings resilience testing, self-assessments, and incident reporting requirements to the hyperscalers themselves, reframing cloud concentration from a bank procurement issue into a matter of systemic financial stability.

title: Coinbase shares slip after Q2 results despite prediction markets doubling and record trading market share
blurb: Coinbase shares fell roughly 7% in after-hours trading after Q2 results, even as prediction-market revenue more than doubled quarter over quarter and its share of global crypto trading volume hit a record 10.3%. The company said 88% of net revenue now comes from outside bitcoin spot trading, with subscription and services revenue reaching $555 million and average USDC balances hitting a record $20B.

title: New York sues Kalshi over illegal gambling claims, seeks $36 billion in damages
blurb: New York Attorney General Letitia James sued Kalshi for operating an unlicensed gambling business, seeking a temporary restraining order and at least $36 billion in compensatory damages pending a full accounting. The suit argues Kalshi's event contracts on sports, culture, and elections meet the state's legal definition of gambling, setting up a jurisdictional clash with the CFTC, which moved separately to block New York's enforcement.

title: New York sues Kalshi, alleges it offers a gambling platform 'plain and simple'
blurb: New York's attorney general sued prediction-market platform Kalshi, alleging its event contracts are unlicensed sports and event wagers and asking the state Supreme Court to bar it from operating in New York. The suit, which seeks triple Kalshi's gains plus $100,000 per unauthorized wager offer, adds to mounting state-level legal pressure on prediction markets even as Kalshi targeted a $40B valuation and won a preliminary injunction against a similar ban in Minnesota.

title: Global banks test tokenized money for cross-border payments in $1 million BIS pilot
blurb: The Bank for International Settlements ran Project Agorá, a live pilot in which 28 commercial banks including JPMorgan, Citi, UBS, and Deutsche Bank settled roughly $1M in real cross-border payments across six currencies using tokenized central bank reserves and commercial bank deposits. The 30 transactions cleared in about 80 seconds on a shared ledger, positioning tokenized bank money as a regulated alternative to private stablecoins for interbank and FX settlement.

title: CACHE-UK: A Stability-Aware Memory Editor for Sequentially Updated Quantized LLMs in Finance
blurb: This paper introduces CACHE-UK, a memory-editing framework for keeping 4-bit quantized financial LLMs factually current as regulations, market conditions, and corporate facts change, without the catastrophic forgetting that sinks existing sequential-edit methods under quantization. Tested on a 4-bit OpenLLaMA-3B model over 88,021 UK financial documents, it cut knowledge degradation by 11-17% and lifted generalization to 28%, a 6-point gain over the strongest baseline, though absolute accuracy stays low.

title: Remitly launches Global Card to turn cross-border money transfers into everyday banking
blurb: Remitly launched the Global Card, a Visa debit card and multi-currency account that lets cross-border customers get paid, spend, and send money home from a single balance in US dollars or USDC. The card is issued through Lead Bank with the wallet powered by Stripe and funds held at Fifth Third Bank for pass-through FDIC insurance, extending Remitly beyond remittances into everyday banking for immigrant and underbanked workers.

title: Coinbase shares fall after crypto exchange posts disappointing second-quarter results
blurb: Coinbase reported a Q2 loss of $359.5M, or $1.36 per share, against a 17-cent loss expected, its third straight quarter missing Wall Street on both revenue and earnings as crypto trading stayed soft. Subscription revenue of $555M grew as a share of the $1.2B total, offering evidence its diversification push is taking hold even as shares fell more than 7% after the bell.

title: Senators may toughen Trump concession on Clarity Act's limits
blurb: Senators Thom Tillis and Ruben Gallego have finalized a bipartisan rewrite of the Clarity Act's ethics section, aiming to tighten the narrow conflict-of-interest limits Trump agreed to accept on his crypto ventures. The revised language still needs White House sign-off and Democratic buy-in before the digital-asset market structure bill can reach a Senate floor vote ahead of the August recess.

title: APEX-Accounting
blurb: APEX-Accounting, a closed benchmark from Mercor and Ramp, tests whether frontier models can do real accounting work like reconciling accounts, accruing expenses, and posting transactions across 160 expert-authored tasks. Claude-Fable-5 leads at 56.4% Mean Criteria@3, but no model clears 2.6% on Pass^8, meaning none reliably completes a full task eight times running. For fintech teams eyeing automated bookkeeping, the results show frontier models still fall short of unsupervised ledger work.

title: Polygon Turns Kansai Electric Loyalty Points Into JPYC Spending
blurb: Kansai Electric's MOACT rewards app now lets users convert NORM loyalty points into JPYC, Japan's first FSA-registered yen stablecoin, on Polygon, with the balance landing in users' own HashPort Wallets and connectable to DeFi. The integration turns an expiring closed-loop Web2 liability into an onchain asset and extends a JPYC run that already includes Diners Club point conversions and a KDDI stablecoin payment pilot at Lawson stores.

title: US Sanctions Iranian Marine Insurers Taking Bitcoin for Strait of Hormuz Passage
blurb: The US Treasury's OFAC sanctioned two Iranian firms, HormuzSafe Marine Services and the Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company, for forcing commercial vessels to buy IRGC-backed "insurance" to transit the Strait of Hormuz, with HormuzSafe accepting Bitcoin and other digital assets to evade sanctions. The designations under Executive Order 13902 block the firms' US-held property and expose non-US counterparties to secondary sanctions, extending a pattern of Iranian state entities routing to crypto rails as banking channels close.

title: Strategy books $8.2 billion Q2 loss on bitcoin price decline
blurb: Strategy reported an $8.2B second-quarter net loss, driven almost entirely by an $8.32B unrealized markdown on its 843,775 bitcoin under fair-value accounting, now worth $54.8B against a $63.7B cost basis. Facing scrutiny over its preferred-stock and convertible-debt structure, the firm has built a $3.75B cash reserve covering 2.1 years of dividends and begun selling bitcoin under a new monetization program.

title: South Korea plans to tax crypto gains over $1,740 as political battle moves to parliament
blurb: South Korea will begin taxing crypto gains above 2.5 million won (roughly $1,740) at a 22% combined rate on Jan. 1, 2027, ending a run of delays that had pushed the measure back three times since 2022. Critics in the opposition warn that the absence of loss carry-forwards could dampen domestic demand and drive investors toward offshore exchanges and P2P markets, and a competing bill to abolish the tax is now before parliament.

title: Mastercard spent decades training its fraud system to see bots as thieves. Now bots are the ones doing the buying.
blurb: Mastercard is rewriting the risk rules it spent decades building to block bots, after AI-driven agentic commerce turned automated buyers into legitimate customers rather than fraud signals. Chief AI officer Greg Ulrich said the network, which scores 175 billion transactions a year in under 100 milliseconds, must now let approved bots transact, a shift that reshapes fraud modeling for the entire payments ecosystem.

title: Lloyds Bank bets on AI to cut £2bn in costs by 2030 as profits jump
blurb: Lloyds Banking Group unveiled "Accelerate 2030," a plan to cut £2bn in costs by decade's end using AI, targeting a cost-to-income ratio below 45% from around 50% today. The push arrives alongside a 23% jump in half-year pre-tax profit and follows 1,600 role cuts in early 2024, though CEO Charlie Nunn declined to say whether the AI drive will trigger fresh redundancies.

title: Revolut to offer ChatGPT subscriptions in OpenAI deal
blurb: Revolut will give retail customers free access to OpenAI's ChatGPT Go, bundling the £7-per-month tier into its paid subscriptions across the UK and EU. Metal and Ultra users get 12 months free, while the two cheaper plans include three and six months respectively, extending Revolut's push to make its subscriptions a lifestyle bundle rather than a pure banking product.

title: Can Large Language Models Execute Parent Orders?
blurb: This paper presents PACE (Plan-Ahead Controlled Execution), the first systematic study of using LLMs for parent-order execution, splitting large orders into smaller ones to cut trading costs without market assumptions or task-specific training. On Shenzhen Stock Exchange Level-1 data, PACE beat TWAP, Almgren-Chriss, and learning-based baselines by 0.65 bps. The authors also found LLMs execute differently from humans: higher model confidence predicted better performance, and the model traded earlier rather than waiting toward the deadline.

title: Judge blocks Minnesota ban on prediction markets
blurb: A federal judge granted a preliminary injunction blocking Minnesota's SF 3432, the first state law to ban prediction markets, letting Kalshi and Polymarket keep operating in the state pending trial. Judge Katherine Menendez found the platforms likely to win on their claim that the Commodity Exchange Act preempts state authority, reinforcing that event contracts fall under CFTC jurisdiction rather than state gambling regulators.

title: JPMorgan says crypto bill’s fading odds hurt outlook, warns parts could discourage institutional adoption
blurb: JPMorgan analysts said the fading odds of the Clarity Act clearing the Senate before year-end are a setback for crypto markets, downgrading their near-term outlook. They warned that specific provisions in the bill, as drafted, could discourage institutional adoption rather than encourage it, complicating the regulatory clarity banks and asset managers have been waiting on.

title: New York sues Kalshi for alleged violations of its gambling laws; the CFTC files an emergency motion to stop the state's enforcement, calling it an "overreach" (Jonathan Stempel/Reuters)
blurb: New York sued Kalshi under state gambling laws, and the CFTC responded with an emergency motion to block the state's enforcement, calling it regulatory overreach of its exclusive authority over the prediction-market platform. The clash sets up a federal-versus-state jurisdictional fight that could determine whether event contracts are regulated as CFTC-overseen derivatives or as gambling subject to state-by-state licensing.

title: Stripe vet buys a bank for his fintech
blurb: Darragh Buckley, Stripe's first employee and founder of banking-infrastructure fintech Increase, acquired Washington's Twin City Bancorp and rebranded it Increase Bank after winning regulatory approval for the ownership and business-plan changes. Owning the charter gives Increase direct connections to the Federal Reserve, The Clearing House, and Visa, cutting out the sponsor-bank middleware whose failure took down Synapse and stranded customer funds.

title: Ready Shuts Card Program After Issuer Kulipa's Sudden Wind-Down
blurb: Ready, the self-custodial wallet formerly known as Argent, shut down its card program on Wednesday after issuer Kulipa wound down without notice, and Solana wallet Solflare's card failed the same way. Kulipa, which had raised a $6.2M seed four months earlier and ran card programs for roughly 20 crypto wallets and fintechs, cited solvency issues, exposing how many crypto cards share the same handful of rented issuer-processor rails.

title: Hims and Hers shares fall 10% as FTC sues company over data, billing practices
blurb: The FTC, joined by Los Angeles County and Utah, sued Hims and Hers for allegedly sharing users' health data with Meta and Snap, billing customers before a provider consultation, and obstructing subscription cancellations, sending shares down 10%. The suit escalates a nearly three-year probe that Hims disclosed a $15M probable-loss accrual for in May, and it puts telehealth's intake-to-prescription billing model under direct regulatory scrutiny.

title: UK’s Markets Regulator Unveils Scope of Data Feed for Stocks
blurb: The UK Financial Conduct Authority set out the scope of a consolidated data feed for equities, defining how much trading data can be published for stocks listed in London. The FCA is betting that cheaper, standardized market data will pull more activity onto the London Stock Exchange and help it compete with US and EU venues for listings and order flow.

title: Coinbase sinks 5% after missing second-quarter revenue estimates
blurb: Coinbase reported $1.22B in second-quarter revenue, down 14% quarter-over-quarter and short of the $1.29B consensus, as a crypto selloff cut industry spot volumes more than 20% and pushed transaction revenue to $599M. Subscription and services revenue reached $555M but also missed estimates, undercutting the company's case that recurring lines can offset trading weakness and sending shares down about 5% after hours.

title: Quantum Solutions, Hyperscale Data tap crypto treasuries to fund AI data centers
blurb: Tokyo-listed Quantum Solutions sold 1,000 ETH for $1.9M, more than doubling its disposal ceiling to fund an AI data center business, while fellow treasury firm Hyperscale Data monetized about 100 BTC and opened a bitcoin-backed credit line at 4.5%-5% for a Michigan AI campus. The moves show crypto treasury firms pivoting their token stockpiles into AI infrastructure spend, even as Quantum booked a loss selling ETH 47% below its acquisition cost.

title: JPMorgan says fading Clarity Act odds weigh on crypto outlook
blurb: JPMorgan said the odds of the Clarity Act passing the Senate this year have fallen to roughly 37% on prediction markets, removing a key catalyst for crypto markets and institutional adoption. The bank warned that continued delay could push tokenization onto incumbent financial infrastructure rather than public blockchains, since Senate negotiations remain deadlocked over DeFi, stablecoin yield, and anti-money laundering provisions.

title: PayPal and Amazon launch BNPL payments for customers in Germany and Austria
blurb: PayPal and Amazon launched buy-now-pay-later checkout for German and Austrian customers, letting shoppers split Amazon purchases into installments or defer payment via PayPal at the point of sale. The rollout extends PayPal's BNPL footprint into Amazon's largest European markets outside the UK, deepening a partnership that already spans wallet and Venmo acceptance across Amazon's US and EU storefronts.

title: US Senate delays crypto Clarity Act as floor time runs short
blurb: The US Senate shelved the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to prioritize floor time for a Russia sanctions bill and federal nominations, pushing crypto's central market-structure effort further down a crowded agenda. With the chamber's summer recess starting August 8 and a contentious provision barring senior officials from backing crypto projects still unresolved, the bill's next realistic window slips to September.

title: MoonPay opens PayBox for AI agent transactions
blurb: MoonPay launched PayBox, a payments product that lets AI agents hold funds and transact on a user's behalf, extending its crypto on-ramp infrastructure into agentic commerce. The move positions MoonPay alongside emerging agent-payment standards from Stripe and Visa, betting that autonomous agents will need programmatic wallets and settlement rails as they begin executing purchases without a human in the loop.

title: Ramp enters Canada
blurb: Ramp launched in Canada, extending its corporate card and spend-management platform beyond the US for the first time as it expands internationally. The move puts Ramp in direct competition with domestic incumbents and neobanks like Float and existing players such as Brex, and signals that US spend-management providers see cross-border expansion as the next growth lever once the home market saturates.

title: Citadel Securities expects surprise Fed rate hike under Kevin Warsh
blurb: Citadel Securities expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates a quarter-point on Wednesday, a surprise move markets are pricing at roughly 40% and one the firm says would end the forward-guidance era under Chairman Kevin Warsh. A hike now would reshape expectations about how the Fed responds to inflation, influencing business pricing and wage demands before price pressures become entrenched.

title: Bernstein sees 78% upside for Robinhood as tokenization, prediction markets expand its crypto business
blurb: Bernstein maintained its $160 price target on Robinhood, implying 78% upside, citing tokenized equities and prediction markets as the next growth engines for its crypto business. The call frames Robinhood's expansion beyond retail brokerage toward on-chain asset trading and event contracts, betting those newer rails deepen crypto revenue as trading volumes and interchange from its core business normalize.

title: X Money launches as Elon Musk advances his “everything app” vision
blurb: X launched X Money, an in-app banking service for Premium subscribers built on partner Cross River Bank, offering peer-to-peer payments, a deposit account with up to 6% APY, and a Visa debit card with 3% cash back and no-fee ATM withdrawals. The rollout, live to a subset of US users, advances Musk's everything-app plan and puts X into direct competition with neobanks and payment apps like Cash App and PayPal.

title: Stablecoins and Cross-Border Payments: How Digital Dollars Move Across Borders
blurb: Stablecoins now move dollars across borders in three legs: an on-ramp that converts local currency to USDT or USDC, an onchain transfer that settles in seconds, and an off-ramp back to local currency. The model sidesteps the correspondent-banking delays and multi-party fees that keep a Friday-afternoon New York-to-Mumbai transfer stuck until Monday. USDT and USDC control over 85% of the market, so most cross-border stablecoin flow still rides on dollar-backed reserves.
